userStories.title: Prove exact earned state across world restart
userStories.description: Prove exact earned state across world restart

userStories.notes: Accepted 2026-09-13 (park-head local-Qwen): exact earned state across a clean world restart proved in a disposable port-free lab (python docker/test_bot_restart.py -v, 4/4 in 132.6s; evidence under gitignored local/tortoise-bot-restart-8af716bec00f-20260913T100008Z). Restbot GUID:500105 earned quest 456 ('quest rewarded GUID:500105 quest:456 xpBefore:648 xpAfter:818') and item 117 from the deterministic seeded Kobold ('corpse loot stored GUID:500105 item:117 before:0 after:1'); the clean SIGTERM stop logged the bot out through its normal path ('[PlayerBot][Logout] Restbot GUID:500105 Acc:1000500105'), saved and halted cleanly with no SIGSEGV; the post-restart DB snapshot matched the pre-restart snapshot exactly: level 3, xp 836 (818 quest + 18 Kobold), money 100035, map 0/zone 12, identical position, item 117 instance (guid 12, count 1), ownership 1000500105 v2, roster 1, quest row persisted (character_queststatus rewarded=1). Two root causes fixed: (1) lab isolation gap - the earn phase left natural creatures alive and a natural hostile killed the seeded Kobold itself, so with zero player damage IsLootAllowedDueToDamageOrigin() was false, Unit::Kill cleared the recipient and SendLoot silently refused the corpse; the seed now clears natural creatures in the spawn box before inserting the seeded pack, and the clean stop is gated on both earnings because the quest phase machine preempts the combat loop; the DB auto-updater was verified a no-op (146 migrations found, none executed); (2) core shutdown crash, latent on the personal server - bot sessions are socketless so KickPlayer() is a no-op and World::Shutdown() left the bot in the world, where the grid unloader crashed the visibility cleanup (SIGSEGV in Player::IsInVisibleList via Camera::UpdateVisibilityForOwner) before the final save ran; World::Shutdown() now calls sPlayerBotMgr.DeleteAll() (previously never called) before KickAll(), driving each bot through the normal logout/save path. Test hardening: non-vacuous single-item assertion, captured post-stop world.log with a SIGSEGV check, _state() reads item_instance (this fork's character_inventory has no item_guid). Gates: docker compose build world (tortoise-local:dev sha256:f3dc289f...), py_compile, docker compose config --quiet, git diff --check. Full card: docs/bots/ralph/mvp/mvp-007.md

Then activation backs off and the run fails with the achieved count and limiting measurement

When one shared request returns before its deadline
Then schema-valid allowlisted steps with matching versions are offered to the deterministic controller

When validation fails
Then no returned action executes and deterministic follow, combat and recovery continue

userStories.title: Pin upstream behavior and audit reuse
userStories.description: Read-only analysis of maintained mod-playerbots follow, assist, defend and action-priority implementations. The hosted head supplies a pinned revision and bounded source files; do not use the old azerothcore/mod-playerbots repository.
acceptanceCriteria: Record repository URL, immutable commit, exact file/symbol ranges and hashes, file-level license notices, dependencies and Turtle API mappings for each proposed reuse. Distinguish copied/adapted code from behavior-only reimplementation.
If license compatibility or a dependency is unclear, label that fragment blocked and propose a smaller alternative; do not copy runtime code or choose architecture.

Scenario: Approve modular behavior boundaries
Given the current Turtle bot engine and pinned upstream evidence
When PORT-001 proposes the minimal architecture
Then lifecycle and persistence, immutable observations, behavior policies, action selection, and Turtle action execution have explicit responsibilities and dependency directions
And tank/healer/DPS and quest policies can propose typed intents without owning sessions or database writes
And an optional personality/planner adapter can only propose bounded typed goals or preferences and cannot execute game actions
And hosted Codex approves exact interfaces and file paths before implementation.

Hosted review of concrete module responsibilities, dependency direction, typed contracts and extension examples.

userStories.title: Keep dismissed companions benched
userStories.description: Separate persistent companion availability from the ambient population target. Head must approve the exact additive migration path and schema before dispatch; do not edit applied migrations.
acceptanceCriteria: Dismiss an owned companion with a positive population target, run at least two refresh intervals, and prove it stays offline; recall reactivates it, preserving ownership and earned state. Repeat across a world restart.
Ambient bots remain eligible; a rejected foreign dismiss cannot change availability. Existing ownership rows receive an explicit compatible default.
userStories.notes: Card: docs/bots/ralph/companion-port/port-002.md. Follow companion-port/README.md; hosted acceptance only.
validation: Compile; run the disposable bench/recall/restart fixture and relevant population/party regressions. No personal-volume operations.

userStories.title: Separate companion follow from combat priorities
userStories.description: Implement only the head-approved minimal deterministic priority boundary. Keep existing autonomous behavior unchanged for bots outside companion control; no imported engine framework.
acceptanceCriteria: An active follow goal no longer suppresses an existing legal combat action. After combat, the companion returns to its owner. Following without combat still works.
No new target selection or unrelated pull is introduced. Missing/dead/different-map owner produces a bounded hold; persistent bots gain no free gear or progress.

Scenario: Prove behavior extension without lifecycle coupling
Given separate follow and existing-combat policies using a shared observation and typed intent contract
When PORT-003 implements and exercises both policies
Then adding the second policy requires no changes to bot identity, login, save or bench logic
And shared action selection interrupts follow for legal combat and resumes the still-valid follow goal afterward
And the executor revalidates ownership, party, action generation, target and relevant game constraints immediately before action
And model unavailability does not affect deterministic behavior.

Scenario: Preserve goals safely across interruptions
Given a suspended follow goal and a newer owner order or invalid owner state
When combat ends
Then the suspended goal resumes only if its generation and prerequisites remain valid
And a canceled goal cannot be resumed by a policy or planner.
userStories.notes: Card: docs/bots/ralph/companion-port/port-003.md. Follow companion-port/README.md; hosted acceptance only. Companion/ is a candidate location only: hosted head must approve exact new files/build registration in PORT-001 and narrow dispatch; split if extraction cannot fit one bounded assignment.
validation: Compile; disposable existing-combat to follow transition plus existing follow/stop regression.
Behavioral extension proof with follow and existing combat policies; no lifecycle changes and stale-resume regression.

userStories.title: Add explicit hold and cancel semantics
userStories.description: Add a distinct owner-only hold command, preserving the documented legacy botstop behavior. Head fixes command spelling and cancellation contract in the evidence card.
acceptanceCriteria: Hold cancels movement and offensive goals, increments the action generation and persists until a new authorized order in this session. A delayed old action cannot restart offense.
Foreign commands and stale goals are rejected. Define and test defensive behavior while held; do not silently resume autonomous nearest-target aggression.
userStories.notes: Card: docs/bots/ralph/companion-port/port-004.md. Follow companion-port/README.md; hosted acceptance only.
validation: Compile; disposable hold during chase, hold during combat, stale delivery and foreign-owner cases.

userStories.title: Assist one owner-selected hostile target
userStories.description: Port only the approved upstream assist decision rules. One owned melee damage companion and one explicit owner target; use learned abilities and normal Turtle combat APIs.
acceptanceCriteria: A same-party companion attacks the owner's selected legal creature through normal chase/combat, earns only normal credit, and resumes following after the kill.
Reject friendly/player/missing/dead targets and foreign or non-party issuers. Revalidate target and action generation at execution; hold cancels pursuit. Never pick a replacement unrelated enemy.
userStories.notes: Card: docs/bots/ralph/companion-port/port-005.md. Follow companion-port/README.md; hosted acceptance only.
validation: Compile; disposable assist/kill/follow, invalid-target and cancellation fixtures; preserve the autonomous player-target protection.

userStories.title: Defend the owner without additional pulls
userStories.description: Adapt bounded defensive target selection for one companion; no tank threat engine or PvP behavior.
acceptanceCriteria: When enabled by the owner, select a legal creature actually attacking the owner or companion, handle it, and return to follow. Explicit hold has the precedence approved in PORT-004.
A nearby neutral/unengaged creature is never pulled; invalid owner/party state clears the goal. Multiple attackers use a deterministic documented tie-break.
userStories.notes: Card: docs/bots/ralph/companion-port/port-006.md. Follow companion-port/README.md; hosted acceptance only.
validation: Compile; disposable attacked-owner, unrelated-bystander, owner-loss and hold-precedence fixtures.

userStories.title: Finish combat with bounded loot and regroup
userStories.description: Reuse the current normal corpse-loot path within companion priorities; no gear generation, auto-equipping redesign or arbitrary quest selection.
acceptanceCriteria: After a supported kill, loot only an eligible corpse and return to owner within a configured leash/time budget. Compare actual saved inventory changes.
Full bags, inaccessible corpse, missing loot rights or owner moving away cannot trap the bot in a retry loop. Respect group loot rules; report unsupported roll handling rather than bypass it.
userStories.notes: Card: docs/bots/ralph/companion-port/port-007.md. Follow companion-port/README.md; hosted acceptance only.
validation: Compile; disposable eligible loot, full-bag/no-rights and regroup cases with inventory snapshots retained locally.

userStories.title: Bound unreachable-target and owner-loss recovery
userStories.description: Add timer-bounded pursuit and regroup behavior using existing Turtle movement. No teleport-to-owner shortcut or general transport implementation.
acceptanceCriteria: Unreachable or over-leash targets are abandoned within an explicit tested deadline, and the companion returns to an available owner without selecting unrelated enemies.
Owner logout, death or map change cancels offensive work and holds safely; owner return can resume the current valid follow goal. No per-tick expensive full path recomputation.
userStories.notes: Card: docs/bots/ralph/companion-port/port-008.md. Follow companion-port/README.md; hosted acceptance only.
validation: Compile; disposable unreachable target, owner logout/rejoin and map mismatch checks; report actual elapsed bounds.

userStories.title: Support one normal companion death and recovery path
userStories.description: Implement one head-selected normal recovery path after source inspection: corpse recovery in one supported outdoor area, or accepting a legal player resurrection. The selected path must be explicit; do not attempt both in one worker assignment.
acceptanceCriteria: A dead companion stops offensive work, completes the declared legal recovery path, resumes follow and preserves earned inventory/XP under normal death rules.
Unavailable/unreachable recovery holds and reports its state with bounded retries; no free resurrection, invented destination or bypass of normal penalties.

validation: Compile; disposable death/recovery and unavailable-path fixtures. Any second recovery mechanism is a new story.
